findings.defect: Correct, but presented at a depth it does not have, and with the one attribution that matters missing. For a deformed CUBE — which is every family in its own table (Klee-Minty, Chvatal, Goldfarb-Sit) — the entire content is one line: a d-edge joins (x_<d, l_d) to (x_<d, u_d) with l_d < u_d, so the objective changes by c_d(u_d - l_d), a sign independent of x_<d; i.e. the last coordinate is COMBED, one bottom-antipodal step enters the facet it points to, and the facet is again a deformed cube of dimension d-1 with an induced linear objective. 'Combed' and 'recursively combed' USOs are standard terminology in the USO literature (Szabo-Welzl; Schurr's thesis) and the observation that deformed products yield combed LP orientations is, from memory and unchecked against any source, folklore there — it is the standard reason nobody expects long product-structured walks. The route attributes the DEFINITION to Amenta-Ziegler and the cubes to Klee-Minty / Chvatal / Goldfarb-Sit, but presents the combedness and its bottom-antipodal consequence as new and unlabelled. By this project's own standing rule that is a defect, and it is the sixteenth such case if left unfixed. The multi-dimensional-factor generalisation (the normal-fan lemma) is the only part that needs an argument, and it buys nothing: no known construction uses factors of dimension > 2.
findings.evidence: I checked the proof step by step (fibre = {y_k : C_k y_k <= d_k + D_k y_<k(w)}, same facet normals hence same normal fan; edge direction spans ker of the n_k-1 common tight rows, sign fixed by the relaxed row; sink face projects affinely and bijectively onto the shorter deformed product; induction) — it is correct. I also re-tested it independently in exact rationals on 210 random deformed cubes of dimensions 2..7 built by my own generator (random affine l_i,u_i, random objective, all values distinct): the last coordinate was uniform in every one and h_BA <= d in every one, 0 violations. The one-line proof above is what my test measures.

findings.result_name: hcube:blowbest (how high a Holt-Klee blow-up can go)
findings.defect: The route's own scan finished AFTER the report was written and refutes the proposition's gloss. logs/zcor2.log now reads 'dim 4 -> 6: 7963 Holt-Klee blow-ups, best height 12', witness seed [5,8,15,14,9,12,11,10,13,4,7,6,2,3,1,0] (height 5) with z = 15 = 1-bar. So the sequence is 4, 6, 8, 12 at dimensions 3,4,5,6 — NOT '+2 per dimension, that is, linear' — and at dimension 6 the blow-up TIES the best Holt-Klee height known there (h*_HK(6) >= 12), so 'B falls short of the Holt-Klee ceiling' is established only at dimension 5 (8 < 11). The substantive conclusion survives and should be restated as the real one: 12 < 2*h*_HK(4)+2 = 14, so B still does not witness (G1), and the Holt-Klee outputs are never parity-good enough to seed again, so there is no HK-preserving ITERATION.

findings.result_name: hcube:dprod / rem:hcube-notallcubes — what the theorem can bind
findings.defect: The theorem provably does not touch the target, and the route's own corollary says so: the occupancy polytope of a length-6 one-player game at m=4 is not a deformed cube, because a uniform coordinate forces h_BA <= 1 + h*(m-1) = 5 < 6. So the class the theorem closes is disjoint from the objects of interest at the smallest size where anything happens. It is also not a barrier in this document's sense: it covers NONE of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi. It belongs in the same category as prop:auso-size — a no-go for one construction technique on the pivot side — and must be labelled as such rather than as a barrier. One further caveat the route should carry: 'the whole classical arsenal' rests on the unchecked memory that Amenta-Ziegler show the known long-path cubes to be deformed products; the MODERN arsenal for long policy-iteration / simplex runs (Friedmann 2011, Fearnley 2010, Christ-Yannakakis 2023) is built from GAMES, not from deformed products, and is excluded from the pivot by its Theta(n) actions per state, not by this theorem.
findings.evidence: rem:hcube-notallcubes in the route's hcube.tex; h*(3)=4 is prop:auso-census; the m=4 length-6 one-player games are rem:hk-survey in frontier.tex, which I re-verified are Holt-Klee AUSOs of height 6 (56 such classes, from my own scan of census/classes4.txt).

findings.defect: Not new as facts — the paper already records them as computations: rem:D-quadratic says 'from dimension 5 on its products violate Holt-Klee, so by prop:oneplayer-lp no nondegenerate one-player game realises them, and any realisation must use both players', and the passage before prop:b2-realised says the second level 'is not Holt-Klee, so any realisation needs Min vertices or ties'. What IS new, and is the route's most useful contribution, is the PROOF and its generality: cor:hcube-transl gives, for every level and every dimension, that a blow-up whose translation vector is a single outer coordinate of the previous level fails Holt-Klee, hence B^k for every k >= 2 needs Min vertices or ties. The write-up does not say plainly that this is measurement-to-proof, and it should. One presentational point: 'the two source-sink edges are opposite edges of the square' must be read as 'distinct parallel edges' — with that reading rule (b) is exact.

findings.result_name: rem:hcube-gap (G1) — the gap is stated loosely
findings.defect: (G1) conflates a numerical inequality with the existence of an operation. The inequality h*_HK(m+2) >= 2 h*_HK(m) + 2 for all m ALONE gives h*_HK(m) >= 2^{m/2+1} - 2 by induction; no operation is needed, and demanding one makes the gap look harder than it is while making it a weaker target. Also (G1) is only a proxy: even h*_HK exponential would not give a one-player family, since realisability at polynomial size is a separate and undecided question (prop:auso-size, and at m=4 the coincidence of Holt-Klee with one-player realisability is a measurement with five holes).

verdict: MEANS SOMETHING, BUT LESS THAN IT SAYS, AND TWO OF ITS FOUR HEADLINE ITEMS ARE ALREADY IN THE PAPER. Nothing here is wrong: every proof I checked is correct and every exhaustive computation I re-ran with independently written code reproduced exactly (3-cube census 744/728/656; 4-cube census and its 56 Holt-Klee height-6 classes with none at height 7; the parity tables; both stacking rules; the Klee-Minty outmap and heights; the h*_HK(5)=11 witness; the m=5 and m=6 games from the rows printed in the write-up; levels 1 and 2 of the blow-up; 210 exact deformed cubes). But the significance breaks down as follows. (1) hcube:hkfive is prop:hkfive, already in frontier.tex with the same witness, with a cleaner proof; do not integrate twice. (2) hcube:oneplayer at m<=4 is cor:hstar-one, already there and STRONGER (ties allowed, via thm:no-seven); only the m=5 and m=6 games are new, and their real value is one the route missed — they show the paper's own 'h*_1(k)-k <= 2' pattern behind cor:gate stops at k=4 (h*_1(5)-5 >= 4, h*_1(6)-6 >= 6). (3) The main theorem is correct but shallow and under-attributed: for deformed CUBES, which is its whole table, it is the one-line observation that the last coordinate is COMBED (sign(c_d)(u_d-l_d) is constant), and combed/recursively-combed USOs are standard USO-literature vocabulary; that sentence must be added, flagged from memory. Worse, its own corollary proves the class it closes is disjoint from the objects of interest already at m=4, and it covers none of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi — it is a no-go for one pre-1999 construction technique (the modern arsenal, Friedmann/Fearnley/Christ-Yannakakis, is built from games, not deformed products), and should be labelled that way rather than as a barrier. (4) Its one substantial new proof is the blow-up analysis: lem:hcube-blowfaces + cor:hcube-parity + cor:hcube-transl turn two of the paper's per-dimension MEASUREMENTS into a general theorem — every blow-up level k >= 2 fails Holt-Klee, hence (prop:oneplayer-lp) needs Min vertices or ties, for ever. That is worth having, and it dovetails with prop:b2-realised, which realised level 2 with one Min vertex. (5) One reported claim is refuted by the route's own log, which finished after the report: the best Holt-Klee blow-up at dimension 6 has height 12, not the '+2 per dimension, linear' the proposition glosses (4,6,8,12), and 12 ties the best Holt-Klee height known at m=6; the proposition must be restated before it goes anywhere near the paper. THE TRUE REMAINING GAP, more precisely than (G1): nothing in this route bounds h*_1 or h*_LP from above at any m >= 5, so it leaves untouched the only statement that matters — whether there is a family of one-player stopping SSGs on poly(m) vertices whose all-switches runs are superpolynomial (Melekopoglou-Condon's open question for Howard's rule with two actions per state) — and its own table 1,2,4,6,>=9,>=12 is equally consistent with Theta(m) and with 2^{Theta(m)}; what it actually accomplishes is to eliminate exactly two candidate constructions for that family (deformed products, and thm:blowup's B inside the Holt-Klee class) and no others, while the live line in the paper is now two-player realisation, where Holt-Klee is not an obstruction at all. INTEGRATION: BETTER, but only in compressed form, roughly 1.5 pages, not 34 KB. Integrate: (a) lem:hcube-blowfaces, cor:hcube-parity, cor:hcube-transl with lem:hcube-stack as support, placed at rem:D-quadratic / prop:b2-realised and explicitly labelled 'measurement now proved, for every level'; (b) the m=5 and m=6 one-player games as two row tables attached to cor:hstar-one and to cor:gate's numerical clause; (c) thm:hcube-dprod as ONE lemma (combed last block) + one theorem + one remark, absorbing the Klee-Minty datum of rem:blowup-measured, with the combed-USO attribution sentence and the 'covers no mechanism' sentence; (d) the CORRECTED blowbest numbers 4,6,8,12 with the dimension-6 witness, as a remark. Do NOT integrate: hcube:hkfive (duplicate of prop:hkfive), hcube:oneplayer at m<=4 (weaker than cor:hstar-one), prop:hcube-lp4 (a definition unfolded, with a redundant example), the Klee-Minty/Chvatal/Goldfarb-Sit table beyond one line, and rem:hcube-five beyond a single sentence recording that the second search was not a discriminator. Also drop next_steps item 4 from the route's plan: thm:no-seven has already closed it.
